what_its_for: Varenicline is a prescription medicine that helps you quit smoking. It works by blocking the good feelings that nicotine causes in your brain, which makes smoking less satisfying. It also reduces cravings and withdrawal symptoms when you stop smoking.
how_to_take: Take varenicline by mouth with a full glass of water (8 ounces). Always take it after eating a meal or snack — this helps prevent an upset stomach and nausea. Swallow the tablet whole. Do not crush or chew it. Take it at the same times each day to help you remember.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over the first week. Days 1 to 3: Take 0.5 mg once a day. Days 4 to 7: Take 0.5 mg twice a day (morning and evening). Day 8 onwards through the end of treatment: Take 1 mg twice a day (morning and evening). You will usually take the full 1 mg dose for 12 weeks. Your doctor may recommend another 12 weeks to help you stay smoke-free. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions, as your dose may be different.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if your next scheduled dose is more than 4 hours away. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store varenicline at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use the medicine after the expiration date on the package.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking too much alcohol while taking varenicline, as it may increase side effects like dizziness and unusual behavior. Be careful driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, since it can cause drowsiness or dizziness. Avoid stopping this medicine suddenly without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, since quitting smoking itself can change how other medicines work in your body.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you experience: thoughts of suicide or self-harm, new or worsening depression or anxiety, unusual changes in mood or behavior, aggression or agitation, seeing or hearing things that are not there (hallucinations), seizures, chest pain, shortness of breath, or signs of a serious skin reaction such as blistering, peeling, or a rash with fever. Also contact your doctor if you have severe nausea, vomiting that does not go away, or if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
when_it_works: Most people start to feel reduced cravings within the first week of taking varenicline. You should set a quit date within the first 1 to 2 weeks of starting the medicine. Some people may need a little more time, so talk to your doctor if you are not ready to quit by then. The full benefit is usually felt after several weeks of taking the full dose. Keep taking it even if you slip up — quitting smoking can take more than one try.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If you have severe kidney disease or are on dialysis, your doctor may prescribe a lower dose. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Varenicline is not recommended during pregnancy or while breastfeeding. Talk to your doctor about safe ways to quit smoking if you are pregnant. Children and teenagers: Varenicline is not approved for anyone under 18 years old. Older adults: Older patients may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness. Be extra careful when standing up or moving around. Mental health history: If you have a history of depression, anxiety, or other mental health conditions, talk to your doctor before starting this medicine, as it requires extra monitoring.
